name: Act of March 3, 1875 funding the perfection of the Eastern Band of Cherokee's title to their North Carolina lands (Qualla Boundary, Royce area 580)
promises: Not a cession: the Act directed that funds appropriated by the act of July 29, 1848 be spent perfecting the Cherokees' title to their lands in North Carolina (Royce).
Royce records that, with the act of August 14, 1876, the bulk of the lands secured to the Indians under this legislation is the Qualla Boundary, with some small detached tracts.
today: NCpedia (State Library of North Carolina) says the Qualla Boundary, about 57,000 acres bought for the Cherokee by William Holland Thomas in the 1840s and 1850s, was found by federal arbitrators in 1874 to belong to the tribe, placed in trust, and surveyed in 1876.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 878-879
Qualla Boundary
sources.publisher: NCpedia, State Library of North Carolina

openQuestions: The Act secured land rather than taking it; no court, claims-commission or government finding that it was broken was found. Eastern Band claims before the Indian Claims Commission concern the 1835 treaty and removal funds and were not read for this record.
The Eastern Band's own website (ebci.com) failed with a certificate error, so its account is not recorded.
The text of the Act was not opened; it is described from Royce.
